newsitem.title: UK: TREASURIES IN LONDON AWAIT CPI ON FIRM GROUND.
newsitem.headline: TREASURIES IN LONDON AWAIT CPI ON FIRM GROUND.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries in London maintained their firmer tone on Thursday after a rollarcoaster ride the previous session following benign U.S. data.
Analysts said further soft data would help the market recover more ground, but sentiment was fragile with U.S. growth still expected to pick up in the third quarter.

Bond prices surged 1-1/4 points in early trade on Wednesday on relief that July retail sales and producer prices were not as strong as feared. But a reversal later was also savage, with the long bond closing at 96-24 in New York after reaching 97-13.
One trader in London said the session was quiet with most of the buying done in the Asian time zone.
By 1000 GMT, the 30-year long bond was quoted at 96-30 to yield 6.61 percent compared with 96-31 in Tokyo. The 10-year note stood unchanged at 98-18 yielding 6.32 percent.

"We'll take the lead from CPI today," said the trader. July consumer prices, due at 1230 GMT, are forecast to rise a modest 0.2 percent in both the headline and core rates after a 0.1 percent rise in June.
"As long as there is nothing untoward in the CPI... I think we should be able to recover further ground," said Rob Hayward, international economist at BankAmerica in London.
"If we get a strong number that will be the end of it," he added. "But I think the risks (for the CPI) probably are on the downside."
Traders said another mild number was unlikely to ignite a sharp rally as most of the short term shorts caught on Wednesday had closed their positions.

July industrial production data, due at 1315 GMT, were unlikely to cause any upsets, analysts said. The consensus forecast according to a Reuters poll was for a rise of 0.2 percent from 0.1 in June, with capacity use expected unchanged at 83.5 percent.
"A 0.5 percent rise or above would be disappointing," said Hayward, adding that a strong number would mainly stem from a volatile component.
In the futures market, the September T-bond contract was up 7/32 on the day at 113-02 in automated trade after setting a thick range between 111-31 and 113-19 on Wednesday.
"It almost set a range yesterday for a longer consolidation. There are buyers below 102 and sellers towards 113.16," said the trader.
Also due on Thursday are weekly jobless claims, June business inventories at 1230 GMT, and July real earnings at 1400 GMT.
